result:
The WRK-SPEC is written, passes `spec-graph validate` with no issues, and is committed as `0314633`. It is at `specs/work/WRK-SPEC-MDM-MEMBER-DEPARTURE-001-la-ficha-que-pierde-un-miembro-se-recalcula.md`. As you asked, I stopped there: it stays `draft` and I didn't invoke writing-plans.

**What the code showed** (the RFC's description was partly off):
- **ForceRule in the pipeline** is the real gap. When a `SOURCE_TO_GOLDEN` rule moves a record out, the losing golden record's `golden_data` and `field_lineage` are never touched.
- **Unmerge** already recomputes the original golden record. It has two defects: source pins are switched off only after the recompute, and the `previous` values in field lineage come from the recompute rather than from what was stored.
- **Review resolution** doesn't move any member today, so there is nothing to fix there yet.
- **Impact is wider than the RFC says.** Matching compares against `golden_data` (FRAG-MDM-MATCH-001), so stale values can also produce wrong matches, not just wrong reads.

**Design:**
- One component in `mdm-ingest-service`, `DepartedMemberRecomputer`, handles the golden record that loses a member. It runs in the same transaction that closes the xref span, split into a read-only `compute` step and a writing `apply` step.
- The unmerge, its preview, and the pipeline ForceRule path all use it, so preview and confirm give the same result.
- **Normal case:** full survivorship over the members still attached.
- **Manual-merge survivor:** only fields whose lineage points at the departed record are re-resolved.
- **No members left:** the record becomes `orphaned` and keeps its data as a historical snapshot.
- **Pins:** pins on the departed record are switched off, except a legacy pin whose id is also used by a remaining member. That one is kept, with a warning.
- **Events** are sent only after the transaction commits.

**Activation:**
- `DOM-MDM-PIPELINE-001@1.23.0`
- `DOM-MDM-SURVIVORSHIP-001@1.10.1`
- `DOM-MDM-LINEAGE-001@1.7.0`
- `PROD-MDM-STEWARDSHIP-001@1.8.0`
- `ARCH-MDM-PERFORMANCE-001@1.8.1`

FRAG-MDM-MATCH-001 is cited as evidence only.

**Gate A1:** 14 attacks, 12 BROKEN. The evidence held on all 12, so I accepted every one and changed the design; each ruling is recorded under `## Adversarial Review` in the WRK-SPEC. The ones that changed the design most:
- **Manual-merge survivor:** it was going to be fully recomputed. It now gets the field-by-field recompute instead.
- **Orphaned record:** it was going to be emptied and announced as an update. It now keeps its data and only triggers cache invalidation.
- **Pins in preview vs. confirm:** the two could disagree, which is why the component is split into `compute` and `apply`.
- **Retries:** a rolled-back retry could have sent duplicate events. Events now go out only after commit.

**Gaps to fix when consolidating:**
- `DOM-MDM-PIPELINE-001 §10.8.4` says a golden record left with no members becomes `absorbed`, but `DOM-MDM-SURVIVORSHIP-001 §3.2` says `orphaned`. I followed §3.2.
- §3.2 says orphaned records don't propagate downstream, but doesn't say whether cache invalidation counts.
- "A member left" isn't listed as a recompute trigger.
- No spec covers what happens to ForceRules, suppressions and open review cases that point at a golden record once it becomes `orphaned`.

**Still to do:**
- Review the spec, then move it to `active` with your `verified` entry.
- Per ADR-011, RFC-PIPE-039 moves to `accepted` when the WRK-SPEC goes `active`.
